topStories.headline: Voters Say Yes to School Tax, Elect New Council and Board Members
topStories.dek: Staunton's Nov. 3 ballot produced a clean sweep: a 1% school-construction sales tax passed, and three seats each on City Council and the School Board were filled.
topStories.body:
Staunton voters turned out on November 3 and settled three contested races while approving a measure that will reshape how the city pays for school buildings. The 1% school-construction sales tax carried 57.1% to 42.9% — roughly 6,299 yes votes to 4,728 no votes — giving the city a dedicated revenue stream that city staff had projected would generate between $5.1 million and $5.4 million a year after grocery and hygiene exemptions. The tax is set to expire in 2046.

In the City Council race, all three incumbents or endorsed candidates prevailed. Billy Vaughn led the field with 34.5% of the vote, followed by Alice Woods at 33.3% and Brad Arrowood at 30.0%. All three will serve on a council that will now have to decide how to allocate the new school-tax proceeds and which construction or renovation projects to prioritize first.

On the School Board, incumbent Kristin Siegel topped that ballot at 30.9%, with Barbara White (21.0%) and Cecilia Carpenter (19.3%) also winning seats. Challengers Fontella Brown-Bundy and Jordan Zipser fell short. The three winners will join the board as it navigates the school-capital planning process made possible by the new tax.

Staunton was among a relatively small number of Virginia localities — primarily independent cities — to approve the school sales-tax referendum statewide on Election Day. Augusta County, which held its own vote on the same question, rejected it by a wide margin.

topStories.headline: A New Lane on I-81 Is Opening This Week Near Staunton
topStories.dek: VDOT will open a third northbound lane between exits 222 and 225 during the week of Nov. 9–13 as part of a $101 million widening project.
topStories.body:
Drivers traveling northbound on Interstate 81 through the Staunton area will have extra room starting this week. The Virginia Department of Transportation announced that a third northbound lane, running from the Route 250 on-ramp at exit 222 to the Route 262 off-ramp at exit 225, is scheduled to fully open to traffic during the week of November 9–13.

The lane addition is one piece of a broader $101 million design-build widening project that has been under construction since fall 2023. In addition to the new northbound lane, the project includes widening five bridges and adding a third southbound lane; overall construction on both directions is expected to continue through summer 2027.

VDOT is reminding motorists that active work zones remain in place even after the new lane opens. Drivers should expect shoulder closures, overnight single-lane closures, and shifts in traffic patterns through the corridor. A 60-mph work-zone speed limit remains in effect in both directions.

topStories.headline: Booker T. Washington Supporters Press Toward a Council Proposal
topStories.dek: After a community meeting last Saturday drew residents to the historic building on West Johnson Street, organizers say they are working toward a formal preservation plan to bring before City Council.
topStories.body:
Community members gathered at the former Booker T. Washington High School on October 31 to talk about the building's future, continuing a civic conversation the city formally opened this fall with two listening sessions facilitated by the consulting firm The Spark Mill. Attendees at the Saturday meeting reflected on the school's history as the only high school available to Black students in the Staunton area for three decades, noting that its roughly 112 students produced notable community leaders despite severe resource constraints.

Organizers said after the October 31 meeting that they plan to keep holding community sessions and intend to develop a comprehensive preservation and renovation proposal to present to City Council. The 1936 Art Deco building at 1114 West Johnson Street has been listed on both the Virginia Landmarks Register and the National Register of Historic Places since 2014, and its revitalization is a named strategic goal in the city's adopted Staunton Plan.

The path forward remains unresolved: no formal proposal has been filed with Council, and no funding decisions have been made. The Booker T. Washington Community Center's Thanksgiving dinner on November 13 will be one of the first public events at the building since the community engagement process ramped up.

events.title: ASC Fall Repertory: Witch, The Tempest, and Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
events.location: Blackfriars Playhouse, 10 S. Market St., Downtown Staunton
events.description: The American Shakespeare Center's fall repertory closes November 14 with three productions in rotation: Jen Silverman's darkly comic Witch, Shakespeare's The Tempest (celebrating the Blackfriars' 25th anniversary), and David Catlin's adaptation of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein. Tickets and showtimes at americanshakespearecenter.com.

events.title: City Council Work Session and Regular Meeting
events.location: City Hall, Rita S. Wilson Council Chambers, 116 W. Beverley St.
events.description: The first City Council meeting since the November 3 election; the newly elected members will not yet be seated, but the sitting council is expected to convene in its usual second-Thursday session. Meetings are open to the public and can also be accessed via Zoom.

events.title: BTW Community Center Annual Thanksgiving Dinner
events.location: Booker T. Washington Community Center, 1114 W. Johnson St.
events.description: The Booker T. Washington Community Center hosts its annual community Thanksgiving dinner, open to neighbors and friends of the center.

events.title: Dark Tales and Haunts of the Queen City — Friday the 13th Edition
events.location: City Parking Garage beside the former Stonewall Jackson Hotel, Downtown Staunton
events.description: A walking-tour event showcasing Staunton's darker history — haunts, legends, unsolved mysteries, and local lore — timed to fall on Friday the 13th.

moreNews.headline: Fire Station 1 Closed for Renovations Through Mid-December
moreNews.body: Staunton Fire & Rescue Station 1 at 500 N. Augusta Street closed to the public on October 29 for interior upgrades including new ground-level flooring and a kitchen remodel. The closure is expected to last 30 to 45 days, with normal operations targeted to resume by December 13. To maintain coverage, Engine 1 is operating out of the Staunton Augusta Rescue Squad building on Coalter Street, and Ladder 1 has relocated to Augusta County Fire-Rescue Station 10 near Walmart. The Jumbo Museum inside Station 1 is also closed for the duration. City officials say emergency response levels will not be affected.

restaurants.name: Maude & the Bear
restaurants.type: Fine-dining tasting menu restaurant and inn
restaurants.description: Named to the New York Times' list of the 50 best restaurants in the United States for 2025, this intimate tasting-menu restaurant is set in a restored 1926 Montgomery Ward kit house led by chef Ian Boden.

restaurants.name: Zynodoa
restaurants.description: Farm-to-table Southern cuisine in a stylish historic downtown building, with an acclaimed wine program and weekend brunch.

restaurants.name: Mill Street Grill
restaurants.type: American grill in a historic flour mill
restaurants.description: Housed in an 1890 flour mill, this beloved Wharf District destination serves steaks, seafood, ribs, and comfort food in an Appalachian-flavored setting with a 40-foot Victorian bar.

restaurants.name: The Shack
restaurants.description: A 26-seat James Beard–recognized destination offering sharable handmade pastas and wood-fired pizzas Thursday through Sunday under chef Michael Skipper.

restaurants.name: Byers Street Bistro
restaurants.type: Casual American bistro with live music
restaurants.description: A lively, colorful Wharf District staple with indoor and outdoor seating, Southern-style American fare, craft beer, and frequent live music on weekends.

restaurants.name: The Depot Grille
restaurants.type: Steak and seafood restaurant in a historic train station
restaurants.description: Set inside Staunton's 1902 train station with original floors, church-pew booths, and an ornate 1918 bar from Albany's Ten Eyck Hotel, serving steak and seafood.

restaurants.name: Chop House Tavern
restaurants.description: Upscale downtown steakhouse led by chef Ryan Zale, offering refined cuts alongside comfort tavern classics in the heart of historic Staunton.

restaurants.name: Queen City Bistro
restaurants.description: An elevated Beverly Street destination with evening wine pairings, late-night dining on weekends, and a private-event-ready rooftop space.

restaurants.name: Cranberry's Grocery & Eatery
restaurants.description: A downtown institution housed in what may be Staunton's oldest commercial building (circa 1758), serving organic wraps, soups, locally roasted coffee, fresh juices, and breakfast seven days a week.

restaurants.name: Yelping Dog Wine
restaurants.description: Family-owned neighborhood wine bar on Beverley Street offering more than 1,500 bottled wines, craft beer, gourmet grilled cheese, and charcuterie boards.

restaurants.name: The Pampered Palate Cafe
restaurants.description: A cozy Beverley Street lunch spot open Tuesday through Saturday serving quiches, house-made soups, salads, and creative sandwiches.

restaurants.name: Blu Point Seafood Co.
restaurants.description: A highly rated downtown seafood spot praised for its clam chowder, hush puppies, fried oysters, and fresh daily catches.

restaurants.name: The By & By Cafe and Beer Garden
restaurants.description: A relaxed downtown gathering spot offering good coffee, a casual menu, and an outdoor beer garden atmosphere in the heart of Staunton.

restaurants.name: Kathy's Restaurant
restaurants.description: A no-frills, locals'-favorite diner on Greenville Avenue serving hearty breakfasts and lunches at wallet-friendly prices.

restaurants.name: Wright's Dairy-Rite
restaurants.description: A beloved Staunton institution since 1952, serving burgers, hot dogs, milkshakes, and daily specials from carhop-style parking stalls.

hotels.name: Hotel 24 South
hotels.description: Originally the 1924 Stonewall Jackson Hotel and a member of Historic Hotels of America, this 124-room downtown landmark features a grand marble lobby, indoor heated pool, and the Magnolia South restaurant.

hotels.name: The Blackburn Inn and Conference Center
hotels.description: A 49-room luxury boutique hotel in a beautifully restored 1828 building — designed by Thomas Jefferson protégé Thomas Blackburn — set on 80 acres just steps from downtown.

hotels.name: Frederick House
hotels.description: A charming 23-room B&B composed of five interconnected historic Victorian houses in the heart of downtown Staunton, offering homemade breakfast and walkable access to all major attractions.

hotels.name: Maude & the Bear Inn
hotels.description: An intimate inn adjoining the acclaimed Maude & the Bear restaurant, set in a restored 1926 kit house north of downtown with an exclusive multi-course breakfast for guests.

hotels.name: Tru by Hilton Staunton
hotels.description: A highly rated contemporary Hilton property offering clean, design-forward rooms at competitive rates near Interstate 81.

hotels.name: Hampton Inn Staunton
hotels.description: A comfortable Hampton Inn off I-81 and I-64 with complimentary hot breakfast, free Wi-Fi, and easy access to downtown Staunton.

hotels.name: Fairfield by Marriott Inn & Suites Staunton
hotels.description: A top-rated Marriott property with complimentary breakfast, modern rooms, and a convenient location near downtown Staunton.

shops.name: Pufferbellies Toys & Books
shops.description: The largest independent toy and book store in the Shenandoah Valley, family-owned since 2006 and located in the Wharf historic district.

shops.name: Made; By the People, For the People
shops.description: A curated downtown gift shop showcasing handmade goods from regional artisans, including jewelry, pottery, home décor, and stationery.

shops.name: Latitudes Fair Trade Store
shops.description: A downtown staple carrying ethically sourced textiles, jewelry, and art from artisans around the world.

shops.name: Billy Opal
shops.description: A fashion-forward clothing boutique at 119 E. Beverley Street showcasing a wide range of designers and regularly hosting pop-ups.

shops.name: Burrow & Vine / Juniper Lane
shops.type: Plant, sustainable lifestyle, and vintage boutique
shops.description: Staunton's original plant and sustainable lifestyle boutique has joined with Juniper Lane in a new shared space at 29 E. Beverley, offering houseplants, sustainable home goods, and curated vintage finds.

shops.name: Heard
shops.description: A curated vintage and secondhand apparel shop at 16 S. New Street that doubles as a community gathering space and streetwear destination.

shops.name: Staunton Antiques Center
shops.description: Over 13,000 square feet of antique and vintage furniture, collectibles, memorabilia, and artwork in the historic McCrory building on West Beverley.

shops.name: Eclectic Retro
shops.description: A Byers Street treasure trove for vintage furniture, home décor, fashion accessories, and quirky nostalgic finds from bygone eras.

shops.name: The Sparrow's Nest
shops.description: A cozy gift shop stocked with seasonal kitchenware, candles, stained glass, paintings, and locally inspired décor.

shops.name: Cranberry's Grocery & Eatery
shops.description: Part café, part health-food grocery, this downtown institution in Staunton's oldest commercial building carries organic foods, local specialty products, and Shenandoah Valley gifts.

shops.name: The Book Dragon
shops.description: A locally owned and operated independent bookshop on West Beverley Street drawing in book lovers with a carefully curated selection and a welcoming atmosphere.

shops.name: Medieval Fantasies Company
shops.type: Handcrafted medieval-themed gifts and home goods shop
shops.description: A unique downtown boutique carrying handcrafted home goods, gifts, and decorative items inspired by medieval artistry and craftsmanship.

artEntertainment.name: American Shakespeare Center — Blackfriars Playhouse
artEntertainment.description: The world's only re-creation of Shakespeare's original indoor Blackfriars Theatre, presenting year-round productions of Shakespeare and classic plays under shared house lighting; this fall's lineup includes The Tempest, Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, and Witch.

artEntertainment.name: Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library & Museum
artEntertainment.description: A comprehensive museum and birthplace complex on Gospel Hill dedicated to the life and presidency of Woodrow Wilson, which opened four new permanent galleries in June 2026 covering 1917–1924.

artEntertainment.name: Camera Heritage Museum
artEntertainment.description: The largest camera museum open to the public in the United States, housing a collection of over 7,000 cameras and 2,500 historical photographs of Staunton and Augusta County, with self-guided, audio, and curator-led tours available.

artEntertainment.name: Frontier Culture Museum
artEntertainment.description: A 200-acre open-air museum featuring a dozen reconstructed historic farms from England, Ireland, Germany, West Africa, and early America, with costumed interpreters on site; note that the indoor visitor center is under construction through 2027.

artEntertainment.name: Staunton Augusta Art Center
artEntertainment.description: Celebrating its 65th anniversary in 2026, this nonprofit downtown art center presents changing exhibits, art classes, and special events year-round.

artEntertainment.name: Sunspots Studios Glassblowing
artEntertainment.description: A working studio and gift gallery in the historic Wharf District where visitors can watch live glassblowing demonstrations and browse colorful hand-blown glass vases, ornaments, and art pieces.

artEntertainment.name: R.R. Smith Center for History & Art
artEntertainment.type: Free community art and history gallery
artEntertainment.description: A free admission gallery in a historic downtown building presenting rotating exhibits of local artists and regional historical collections, with shows that change approximately every three months.

artEntertainment.name: The Artisans Loft
artEntertainment.description: Part gallery and part antique boutique, this upper-floor space on West Beverley showcases a range of vintage and handcrafted goods, local art, salvaged architectural pieces, and repurposed décor.

gymsRecreation.name: Staunton-Augusta YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: A comprehensive community hub offering yoga, aerobics, weights, cardio equipment, a swimming pool, tennis, and child care programs for all ages.

gymsRecreation.name: Phoenix Fitness and Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A women-owned studio offering a diverse schedule of yoga, pilates, barre, aerial yoga, and strength classes with flexible membership packages.

gymsRecreation.name: Planet Fitness
gymsRecreation.description: A Judgment Free Zone gym with extensive cardio and strength equipment at affordable membership rates, open extended hours.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training Staunton
gymsRecreation.description: A community-focused functional fitness studio offering 45-minute team-based high-intensity workouts with a strong local following.

gymsRecreation.name: Queen City Strength
gymsRecreation.description: A locally owned strength-focused gym in Staunton with a wide variety of equipment emphasizing powerlifting and performance training.

gymsRecreation.name: Anytime Fitness
gymsRecreation.description: A well-maintained 24-hour gym with friendly staff and a full range of cardio and strength equipment, accessible to members around the clock.

gymsRecreation.name: Gypsy Hill Park
gymsRecreation.description: Staunton's largest public park, featuring a public golf course, tennis courts, a lake, walking trails, a band shell, and a seasonal train ride — a centerpiece of outdoor recreation in the Queen City.

gymsRecreation.name: Aliquid Training and Performance
gymsRecreation.description: A Staunton training facility focused on performance-oriented strength and conditioning programs for athletes and fitness enthusiasts.
